title: Engineering Skeletal Muscle Tissues from Murine Myoblast Progenitor Cells and Application of Electrical Stimulation
protocol: Isolate murine myoblast progenitor cells or C2C12 cells according to a published protocol.
Store isolated cells in liquid nitrogen.
Thaw cells from liquid nitrogen storage.
Place thawed cells into a 25 cm² Matrigel-coated tissue culture flask.
Add growth medium (GM) consisting of DMEM advanced, fetal bovine serum, HS, penicillin/streptomycin, L-glutamin, and chicken embryo extract to the flask.
Coat the tissue culture flask with Matrigel for 2 hours at room temperature before adding cells.
Remove excess Matrigel by aspiration after cell addition.
Subculture cells approximately 1:3 every 3 days.
Passage cells from one 25 cm² flask to a 75 cm² flask on day 3.
Passage cells from one 75 cm² flask to two 150 cm² flasks on day 6, with 30 min preplating in uncoated flasks if necessary.
Transfer one 150 cm² flask to a triple 150 cm² flask or three 150 cm² flasks on day 9, preplate again depending on the cells' phenotype if needed.
On day 12, the cells are ready for seeding into a muscle construct.
Mix the "elastomer" with the "curing agent" in a ratio of 10:1 to prepare silicon glue.
Cut approximately 5 mm square segments of Velcro with one triangular side (house-like shape).
Glue the Velcro into the wells of a 6-well culture plate at a distance of about 12 mm between squares.
Ensure only the soft side of the Velcro is facing upwards and that the rooftops face each other.
Apply silicon glue only to the Velcro, avoiding spread throughout the well.
Leave to dry overnight in vacuum oven without heating.
Add 70% EtOH to the wells and incubate for 15 minutes.
Rinse the wells three times with PBS.
Place under UV light for 15 minutes.
Remove all PBS from the wells and Velcro, then place in incubator until use.
Thaw Matrigel solution in refrigerator.
Prepare collagen solution at desired concentration shortly before making constructs.
Dilute stock collagen with sterile 0.02% acetic acid to final concentration of 3.2 mg/ml.
Transthyretin cells and resuspend in GM, then count the cells.
Leave cell suspension in centrifuge tube in incubator.
Add the required amount of collagen stock solution to a tube based on construct numbers (refer to Table 1).
Add 0.5M NaOH to collagen solution until light pink color indicates pH 7.5.
Gently mix by pipetting up and down, avoiding bubble formation.
Add Matrigel to collagen solution and mix very gently but thoroughly.
Finally, add GM to the Collagen/Matrigel mixture as specified in Table 1.
Centrifuge desired amount of cells at 1,000 rpm for 5 minutes.
Remove supernatant.
Adjust the number of cells per construct between 750,000 and 1,250,000.
Resuspend the cell pellet using some gel mixture.
Transfer the resuspended cells into the remaining gel mixture and mix thoroughly without introducing air bubbles.
Take preheated well plates out of the incubator.
Pipette 0.35 to 0.4 ml of the cell-gel mixture into the Velcro first.
Begin pipetting from the center between attachment sites, extending towards the Velcro.
Fill up any gaps between the two Velcro anchors with the remaining gel mixture and pipette around the Velcro pieces.
Check after 5-10 minutes if the gels are solid enough to transfer by gently tapping the dishes and inspecting visually for rigidity.
Carefully place the plates in an incubator once the gels are rigid, typically after ten minutes.
Gently overlay each gel with 4 ml of warm GM after 1-2 hours.
Replace GM with differentiation medium (growth medium without chick embryo extract) after 24 hours.
Replace the medium every 2-3 days thereafter.
On day 7, evaluate mature oriented muscle fibers using staining for cross striation development.
Sterilize electrodes from the Ionoptix plate with 70% ethanol.
Dry the sterilized electrodes under UV in a safety cabinet.
Place the plate with electrodes onto the culture plate containing constructs.
Cover the setup with the lid from the culture plate.
Transfer the setup to an incubator.
Connect the Ionoptix C-pacer with appropriate cables.
Apply stimulation protocol using 4 V/cm, 6 ms pulses at 2 Hz frequency.
Change the culture medium every 24 hours during stimulation.
